'''Igor Mikhailovich Ternov''' ({{langx|ru|И́горь Миха́йлович Терно́в}}; November 11, 1921 – April 12, 1996) was a Russian theoretical physicist, known for discovery of new quantum effects in microscopic particle motion such as ''Dynamic Character of the Electron Anomalous Magnetic Moment'', ''[[Sokolov-Ternov effect|the Effect of Radiative Polarization of Electrons and Positrons in a Magnetic Field]],'' and ''Quantum Fluctuations of Electron Trajectories in Accelerators''.<ref name="imt"/>

==Biography==
Igor Ternov graduated from [[MSU Faculty of Physics|Faculty of Physics]] of [[Moscow State University]] (MSU) in 1951, where he spent his entire career. Igor Ternov was one of the leading experts in the theory of [[synchrotron radiation]]. 

He developed a new field which explained the theory of quantum processes in strong external fields, emerging from exact solutions of relativistic wave equations. He was the chairman of MSU Physical Society, the vice-rector of MSU, the head of [[Quantum mechanics|Quantum Theory]] and of [[Theoretical Physics]] departments of the MSU Faculty of Physics.<ref name="imt">{{cite web| url= http://library.cern.ch/archives/biographies/Ternov_IM-199606.pdf| publisher= [[CERN]] Scientific Information Service| title= Igor M. Ternov| access-date= 2008-07-08| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080411033809/http://library.cern.ch/archives/biographies/Ternov_IM-199606.pdf| archive-date= 2008-04-11| url-status= dead}}</ref>

In 1976 he received the [[USSR State Prize]] (1976) for prediction and development of the effect of radiative polarization of electrons and positrons in a magnetic field. Igor Ternov was a member of the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union|Soviet Communist Party]], a vice-rector and secretary of bureau of Communist Party of the Physics Department of the [[Moscow State University]].
